claims.statement: For a fully observed stochastic hybrid process whose flow excursions remain safe almost surely, if every guard reset has conditional safe-poststate probability at least 1-p given the complete pre-reset history and chosen action, and at most M guards can fire by horizon T almost surely, then the unsafe probability by T is at most 1-(1-p)^M. With edge-specific risks p_e and pathwise edge-count caps M_e, the bound is 1-product_e(1-p_e)^M_e.
assumptions: Well-posed right-continuous hybrid trajectories and no simultaneous-guard ambiguity after a supplied priority rule.
All between-guard excursions stay in their mode safe sets almost surely, or a separate conditional excursion bound is included.
At each guard event, the conditional post-reset probability of remaining safe is at least 1-p_e for every reachable pre-reset state and allowed reset action.
The number of events of each edge by T is bounded almost surely by M_e.
claims.status: internally_derived_elementary_bound; exact and sharp on the stated model; novelty_not_claimed
claims.novelty_boundary: A repeated-conditioning product bound; no novelty or priority claim. It identifies the event-count and conditional-reset information required when a whole-reset kernel is not otherwise solved exactly.

costs.supplied_or_acquired: Guard geometry, pathwise event-count caps or a compensator, and conditional reset-risk bounds over all reachable guard states/actions.
costs.runtime: O(number of distinct edge types) arithmetic once p_e and M_e are certified; kernel learning and certificate synthesis are excluded.
costs.physical: Sensing, reset actuation energy/latency/wear, calibration, and state-dependent kernel acquisition must be separately charged.

claims.falsifier: A model satisfying the stated conditional reset-risk and event-count premises but exceeding the product risk bound.
claims.next_gate: Audit current stochastic hybrid reset literature and derive whether useful state-dependent guard-risk and event-count certificates can be obtained with lower acquisition cost than the exact hybrid Bellman kernel.

claims.statement: The flow-only certificate B(x)=x on the one-mode loop with flow dx/dt=-1 on (0,1], guard {0}, safe set [0,1], and reset x+=1 with probability 1-p or x+=2 with probability p does not certify whole-hybrid risk <=1/2: at T=M, the exact unsafe probability is 1-(1-p)^M, which is 3/4 at p=1/2 and M=2.
assumptions: A reset to x=2 is unsafe and absorbing.
A reset to x=1 starts the next unit-time flow cycle.
Reset outcomes have conditional unsafe probability p on each visit.
claims.novelty_boundary: This refutes only flow-only transfer. Guard/reset conditions are already present in deterministic hybrid barriers; stochastic scheduled-reset barriers also account for resets.

costs.model: One exact continuous flow, one guard, one Bernoulli reset kernel, one fully observed state.
costs.event_count: Exactly M guard opportunities occur by horizon T=M; dwell time is one, so the model is non-Zeno.

claims.falsifier: No falsifier under the exact stated model; an error in the reset event semantics or probability calculation would invalidate the example.
claims.next_gate: Use as a unit-test model for any proposed stochastic guard-aware certificate or abstraction; verify that it rejects the flow-only claim and recovers the exact loop probability.
